cards.title: Bring your agent code. Foundry runs it.
cards.body: Package any framework as a container. Foundry gives it a dedicated Entra identity and endpoint, per-session isolation and scale to zero.
cards.loop: Every agent passes a hosted checkpoint (JSON, SSE and traces) before the app is built.

link.label: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service

cards.title: From sample to hosted agent with azd ai agent
cards.body: init starts from a sample, run tests it locally, azd deploy builds it in Foundry, invoke calls it and monitor streams its logs. Needs azd 1.32.0 or later.
cards.loop: Copilot runs, deploys and probes every hosted agent with these commands.

cards.title: One framework for agents and workflows
cards.body: The successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen: simple agents for open-ended tasks, graph-based workflows when you need explicit control.
cards.loop: Chosen for basic agents and explicit workflows. One framework per agent.

cards.title: Embed Copilot's agent runtime in your app
cards.body: The engine behind Copilot CLI: planning, tool calls, custom agents and skills. With BYOK it runs on Foundry models, no Copilot subscription needed.
cards.loop: Chosen for agents that load skills at runtime.

cards.title: Chain turns by ID instead of resending history
cards.body: One stateful API that unifies chat completions and Assistants. Stream output, call functions and remote MCP servers, and run long tasks in background mode.
cards.loop: Hosted agents speak Responses; the checkpoint proves JSON and SSE end to end.

link.label: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.title: Define tools once, serve them from one MCP endpoint
cards.body: Toolbox centralizes auth, guardrails, observability and versioning. Any MCP client can connect, and tools change without agent code changes.
cards.loop: Agents reach their tools, MCP servers and skills through one toolbox endpoint.

link.label: What is Toolbox in Microsoft Foundry?

cards.title: Ground agents in your data, with citations
cards.body: Knowledge bases span Blob, SharePoint, OneLake and the web. Agentic retrieval runs parallel subqueries, enforces user permissions and cites sources.
cards.loop: Grounding goes through the toolbox, with a tested answer for insufficient evidence.

cards.title: Let a router choose the model for each prompt
cards.body: One deployment picks the most suitable model for each prompt in real time. Choose Balanced, Cost or Quality mode and an optional model subset.
cards.loop: Available in East US 2 and Sweden Central; Copilot checks region availability first.

cards.title: Unit tests for agents, scored Pass/Fail
cards.body: Built-in evaluators score end-to-end outcomes (Task Adherence, Intent Resolution) and each step (Tool Call Accuracy, Tool Selection). Several are in preview.
cards.loop: Verify scores 10+ spec scenarios and needs a 0.8 pass rate by default.

cards.title: Shift left: attack your agent before you deploy
cards.body: The AI Red Teaming Agent runs automated adversarial scans with open-source PyRIT, scored by Attack Success Rate. Cloud runs add agent risks such as sensitive data leakage.

cards.title: Put guardrails on tool calls, not just chat
cards.body: Agent guardrails (preview) check user input and output, plus tool calls and tool responses, for harmful content and attacks. Hosted agents add egress controls (preview).
cards.loop: Foundry guardrails stay on for every agent.

cards.title: Find which step caused the error or latency spike
cards.body: OpenTelemetry traces record inputs, outputs, tool calls, retries, latency and cost in Application Insights. GA for prompt and hosted agents.
cards.loop: A hosted checkpoint needs correlated traces, not just a good response.

cards.title: An Entra identity type built for AI agents
cards.body: Foundry creates Microsoft Entra Agent IDs for your agents. Tool calls use automatic token exchange, so no secrets sit in prompts or code.
cards.loop: Each agent identity gets only the data roles its tools need.

cards.title: Drop the API keys. Use Microsoft Entra ID.
cards.body: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identities, assign the Cognitive Services User role on the Foundry resource, then disable key-based authentication.
cards.loop: No keys or connection strings; Copilot checks RBAC before it deploys.

cards.title: Meet users in Microsoft Copilot and Teams
cards.body: Publishing from the Foundry portal creates the Azure Bot Service resource and Teams app package. Share it with just you instantly, or with your org after admin approval.

link.label: Publish to Microsoft Copilot and Teams

cards.title: Define what and why before deciding how
cards.body: GitHub Spec Kit turns requirements into a spec, plan and tasks, then guides implementation against them. Run each /speckit-* skill in your agent's chat.

cards.title: Define the process in code, let agents do the work
cards.body: Dynamic workflows (public preview) run automated steps and agents in sequence or in parallel, pause at checkpoints for your review, then resume. In the Copilot app, CLI and SDK.
cards.loop: The SDD workflow is one: four phases, independent reviews and approval gates.

cards.title: Keep scoring your agent on live traffic
cards.body: Continuous evaluation scores samples of live traffic. The Agent Monitoring Dashboard (preview) shows token usage, latency, run success rate, eval scores and red team results.

cards.title: After the first build, just type a command
cards.body: AGENTS.md records the build mode and Foundry project, so Chat understands run, test, deploy and add agent without a long prompt.

cards.title: Every verified fix becomes a lesson
cards.body: Copilot records each verified fix in docs/LOOP.md. Ask it to improve the agentic loop to turn recurring lessons into skill and workflow changes you approve.

cards.title: Prototype fast, harden when it sticks
cards.body: When a prototype earns a pilot, Copilot derives a spec from it and continues with the SDD workflow: Specify, Implement, Verify and Deploy behind approval gates.
